Name: Audrey Morehead
Badge: Reading to Write: They Say / I Say
Which version of the They Say / I Say routine (with visual texts or with annotation) feels like the best fit for your students right now? Why?:

The best fit for my students right now using the they say/I say routine would be the annotation. In order to gain a deeper meaning and comprehension of a test I have been considering having students read on their own and then we would come together as a class and read together. I think they would be able to highlight key points more easily when reading on their own and then as we read together it would make engagement and discussion easier for my students.

Describe one way you might adapt the They Say / I Say framework to align with the types of texts your students read most often (e.g., articles, visuals, multimodal texts).:

Depending on the size of the text I could have sentences or phrases already highlighted/underlined and ask my students to write what they think about those parts. This would give a more guided approach to the framework and allow for everyone to be aware of what is being discussed from the reading.

What, if anything, do you need help thinking through as you plan for using They Say / I Say in your classroom?:
